title: Utilization Management Policy — Placement on a RideLink Level of Service and Reassessment
content:
This policy governs which RideLink level of service a member's Non-Emergency Medical Transportation benefit is placed on after the mobility assessment, and how a level is kept current.

## Clauses

1. **Lowest suitable level.** The level of service is the lowest level whose mobility level meets the member's assessed need. From lowest to highest the levels are RideLink Transit Pass, RideLink Mileage Reimbursement, RideLink Ambulatory Sedan, RideLink Door-to-Door Assist, RideLink Wheelchair Van and RideLink Stretcher Van.
2. **Transit first.** A member able to use fixed-route transit within the transit walking distance of RideLink Transit Pass is placed on RideLink Transit Pass.
3. **Household driving.** A member with a household vehicle and driver may choose RideLink Mileage Reimbursement instead of a sedan.
4. **Documented wheelchair use.** Holding an approved or expired Durable Medical Equipment Authorization for a wheelchair, a Prior Authorization record, documents wheelchair use, so such a member qualifies for RideLink Wheelchair Van on that record without a separate wheelchair assessment.
5. **Stretcher certification.** RideLink Stretcher Van needs a physician certification no older than that level's certification validity period on each trip date.
6. **Reassessment.** Each level is reassessed within the level's reassessment period, counted in months from the mobility assessment date, and a reassessment request is completed within the level's mobility assessment period in business days. The old level stays in force until the reassessment is recorded.

The mobility assessment sets the level and makes a benefit in pending assessment status usable; a later reassessment changes the level of an existing benefit.

## Cases

| Hypothetical situation | Result under the clauses |
|---|---|
| The member can walk to a fixed-route stop within the transit walking distance | Placed on RideLink Transit Pass |
| The member needs a sedan but has a household vehicle and driver | May choose RideLink Mileage Reimbursement instead |
| The member holds an expired Durable Medical Equipment Authorization for a wheelchair | Qualifies for RideLink Wheelchair Van on that record, with no separate wheelchair assessment |
| The member holds such an authorization in approved status | Same result as the expired authorization |
| A RideLink Stretcher Van trip date falls when the physician certification is older than the validity period | The certification requirement for that trip date is not met |
| A reassessment request is open but not yet recorded | The member keeps the existing level |

Clause 4 speaks of an authorization for a wheelchair in approved or expired status; an authorization in any other status is not covered by it.
